raw_case_text: A 67-year-old Caucasian female with a past medical history of atrial fibrillation, hypertension, obesity, degenerative knee joint disease, and no documented history of COVID-19 received a first dose of ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccination. The patient had no allergies, no history of immune deficiency, no recent infectious disease, and denied illicit drug use. Two weeks after vaccination, the patient suffered from fever, weakness and arthralgia of the knees, hips and shoulders ( Figure 1A ). After additional 3 weeks, the patient was admitted to a community hospital with stable vital parameters and normal physical examination ( Figure 1A ). Computed tomography (CT) scans of the chest and abdomen revealed reactive mediastinal lymphadenopathy and hepatic steatosis. Infectious endocarditis was excluded by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and repeat blood cultures were all tested negative. Due to elevated IgM titers, IgM gammopathy was suspected but excluded by bone marrow biopsy. Because both, antibiotic treatment with piperacillin/tazobactam and steroids did not improve clinical symptoms with persistent fever and weakness, the patient was referred to our tertiary center three weeks thereafter ( Figure 1A ). A repeat nasopharyngeal swab for SARS-CoV-2 RNA testing by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was negative. Laboratory examination at admission revealed leukocytosis (16,100/microL, reference range: 4,000-11,000/microL), acute kidney injury (serum creatinine: 1.59 mg/dL, reference range: 0.5-1 mg/dL), hyponatremia (127 mmol/L, reference range: 136-145 mmol/L), elevated C-reactive protein (CRP: 97.9 mg/L, reference range: <=5 mg/L) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH: 340 U/L, reference range: 125-250 U/L). During the further disease course, elevated liver transaminase levels including alanine aminotransferase (ALT: 339 U/L, reference range: <=34 U/L), aspartate aminotransferase (AST: 295 U/L, reference range: <=31 U/L), canalicular enzymes gamma-glutamyl transferase (gamma-GT: 469 U/L, reference range: 9-36 U/L), and alkaline phosphatase (AP: 452 U/L, reference range: 40-150 U/L) were detectable ( Figure 1B ). Serological examination excluded hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed diagnosis of pericarditis with circumferential thickening and contrast enhancement of the entire pericardium at late gadolinium enhancement (LGE,  Figure 1C ). Based on these imaging findings, heart involvement with viral pericarditis was suspected. EBV serology was compatible with past infection (anti-EBV-VCA-IgG: positive, anti-EBV-IgM: negative), confirmed by PCR with no detectable EBV-DNA. However, serology of CMV was compatible with active CMV infection (anti-CMV-IgG: >250 IU/mL, anti-CMV-IgM: positive), confirmed by PCR with detectable CMV viremia (415 IU/mL). Based on active CMV infection, oral valganciclovir was initiated (900 mg twice daily,  Figure 1B ). During the further course, clinical symptoms improved, and liver enzymes normalized ( Figure 1A ). This was associated with successful treatment and decrease of CMV viremia (69.8 IU/mL). The patient was transferred to dermatological care for the treatment of allergic dermatitis after the aforementioned antibiotic treatment, a skin biopsy revealed neither auto-immune nor viral cause of the dermatitis. Thereafter, the patient remained free of symptoms and was discharged with recommendation to continue the antiviral therapy for 3 weeks in total ( Figure 1A ). A follow-up visit 54 days after discharge confirmed normal range liver enzymes (ALT: 9 U/L, reference range: <=34 U/L; AST: 27 U/L, reference range: <=31 U/L; gamma-GT: 28 U/L, reference range: 9-36 U/L; AP: 70 U/L, reference range: 40-150 U/L) and absence of CMV viremia (<35 IU/mL). In summary, we here present the clinical course of a patient with CMV reactivation and pericarditis in temporal association with ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccination against SARS-CoV-2.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 67-year-old Caucasian female presented with a 5-week history of persistent fever, generalized weakness, and polyarthralgia of the knees, hips, and shoulders that began 2 weeks after her first dose of the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two weeks after receiving her first dose of the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine, the patient developed persistent fevers, weakness, and large-joint arthralgias. She was hospitalized 3 weeks later at a community hospital where chest and abdominal CT showed reactive mediastinal lymphadenopathy and hepatic steatosis, transesophageal echocardiography and blood cultures excluded endocarditis, bone marrow biopsy excluded IgM gammopathy, and empiric piperacillin-tazobactam plus corticosteroids failed to resolve her symptoms, prompting transfer to a tertiary center 3 weeks later.
subjective.past_medical_history: Atrial fibrillation, hypertension, obesity, and degenerative knee joint disease; no history of prior COVID-19 or immunodeficiency. Received her first ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine dose 2 weeks prior to symptom onset; no drug allergies or illicit substance use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent fever, generalized weakness, knee/hip/shoulder arthralgias, and an antibiotic-associated pruritic rash.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs were stable and general physical examination was unremarkable at initial community hospital admission; she subsequently developed an antibiotic-induced allergic dermatitis rash.
objective.routine_investigations: Tertiary admission labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 16,100/uL; ref 4,000-11,000), acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.59 mg/dL; ref 0.5-1.0), hyponatremia (sodium 127 mmol/L; ref 136-145), elevated CRP (97.9 mg/L; ref <=5), and elevated LDH (340 U/L; ref 125-250), followed by acute cholestatic hepatitis with ALT 339 U/L (ref <=34), AST 295 U/L (ref <=31), GGT 469 U/L (ref 9-36), and ALP 452 U/L (ref 40-150). SARS-CoV-2 PCR, serial blood cultures, HBV, HCV, HEV, and HIV tests were negative; EBV VCA-IgG was positive with negative EBV-IgM and negative EBV-DNA PCR. Cytomegalovirus serology was positive for both anti-CMV IgG (>250 IU/mL) and anti-CMV IgM. Transesophageal echocardiography excluded infective endocarditis.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest and abdominal CT demonstrated reactive mediastinal lymphadenopathy and hepatic steatosis; bone marrow biopsy was unremarkable; skin biopsy confirmed non-viral/non-autoimmune allergic drug dermatitis. Cardiac MRI (CMR) revealed circumferential pericardial thickening and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) diagnostic of acute pericarditis. Quantitative blood CMV PCR confirmed active CMV viremia at 415 IU/mL.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Active cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection/reactivation presenting with acute CMV pericarditis and cholestatic hepatitis in temporal association with ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccination, confirmed by positive anti-CMV IgM, anti-CMV IgG >250 IU/mL, quantitative blood CMV PCR of 415 IU/mL, and circumferential pericardial late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI. Treatment with a 3-week course of oral valganciclovir (900 mg twice daily) resulted in rapid clinical recovery, decline of CMV viral load to 69.8 IU/mL during treatment and <35 IU/mL at 54-day post-discharge follow-up, and complete normalization of liver enzymes (ALT 9 U/L, AST 27 U/L, GGT 28 U/L, ALP 70 U/L).
